title: Hakone vs Nikko: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Hakone for onsen, Mt. Fuji views, and relaxation. Nikko for UNESCO shrines, waterfalls, and hiking. Both are excellent — Hakone if you want to chill, Nikko if you want to explore.

categories.name: Onsen & Relaxation
categories.summary: Hakone's ryokan culture and volcanic hot springs are unmatched. Nikko has onsen too but they're secondary.

categories.name: Cultural Attractions
categories.summary: Nikko's Toshogu Shrine complex is breathtaking UNESCO heritage. Hakone's culture is more museum-based.

categories.name: Mt. Fuji Views
categories.summary: Hakone is the prime spot for Mt. Fuji viewing across Lake Ashi. Nikko has no Fuji views.

categories.name: Hiking & Nature
categories.summary: Both have excellent hiking. Hakone has volcanic terrain; Nikko has forest trails and Kegon Falls.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Nikko is cheaper overall. Hakone ryokans can be pricey, though budget options exist.

categories.name: Getting There
categories.summary: Hakone is closer to Tokyo (85min) vs Nikko (2hrs). Both have efficient rail access.

categories.name: Day Trip Feasibility
categories.summary: Hakone works as a day trip. Nikko is better as an overnight due to distance.

categories.name: Crowds
categories.summary: Toshogu gets crowded but Nikko's trails are quieter. Hakone can be packed on weekends.

categories.name: Food
categories.summary: Both offer local specialties — Hakone's black eggs and kaiseki vs Nikko's yuba tofu dishes.

categories.name: Photography
categories.summary: Hakone wins for Mt. Fuji shots; Nikko wins for ornate shrine details and autumn foliage.

faq.question: Is Hakone or Nikko better for a day trip?
faq.answer: Hakone is better for a day trip — it's only 85 minutes from Shinjuku and the Hakone Free Pass makes it easy to loop through multiple sights in a day. Nikko takes about 2 hours each way, making overnight stays strongly recommended.

faq.question: Which is more expensive, Hakone or Nikko?
faq.answer: Hakone tends to be pricier, especially for ryokan stays which can run ¥20,000-50,000/person. Nikko entry fees add up (Toshogu is ¥1,300) but budget guesthouses run ¥5,000-8,000. Overall Nikko is the budget-friendlier option.

faq.question: Can I do both Hakone and Nikko in one Japan trip?
faq.answer: Yes, and many travelers do. They're in opposite directions from Tokyo — Hakone to the southwest, Nikko to the north — so don't combine them in one day. Dedicate 1-2 nights to each as separate excursions from Tokyo.
